title: Benchmark Opening Keynote: ESS & EV Demand
gist: Video page for Benchmark Chief Research Officer Adam Panayi's 14-minute opening keynote at Benchmark Week 2026 on global EV sales, energy storage deployment and what they mean for raw material consumption. No transcript or figures are given; the rest of the page lists other sessions on copper, ESS, cathodes and critical-minerals capital.

themes.theme: EV and ESS demand keynote (no transcript)

insights.claim: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence's Chief Research Officer Adam Panayi opened Benchmark Week 2026 on Nov 11, 2026 with a keynote on global EV sales, energy storage deployment and their implications for raw material consumption. The page gives no figures or forecasts.
insights.speaker: Adam Panayi, Chief Research Officer, Benchmark Mineral Intelligence
insights.so_what: Benchmark's headline demand view is the base for its raw material balances, but the numbers are only in the video.
insights.quote: Global EV sales, energy storage deployment and their implications for raw material consumption.
insights.locator: Benchmark Opening Keynote: ESS & EV Demand

insights.claim: A Benchmark Week 2026 panel on grid-scale batteries framed energy storage (ESS) as the next demand frontier, covering ESS market growth, which battery chemistries are winning, and the grid infrastructure investment required.
insights.speaker: Adam Panayi, Chief Research Officer, Benchmark Mineral Intelligence
insights.so_what: Benchmark is positioning stationary storage as the next leg of battery raw material demand, relevant to lithium and LFP supply chains.
insights.quote: How the ESS market is growing, which chemistries are winning, and the infrastructure investment the future grid will need.

insights.claim: Benchmark Week 2026 included a Benchmark copper market update framing copper's role in electrification around supply constraints and demand from EVs, grid infrastructure and datacentres.
insights.speaker: Adam Panayi, Chief Research Officer, Benchmark Mineral Intelligence
insights.so_what: Copper demand is being linked to datacentres and grid build-out as well as EVs, broadening the demand case beyond autos.
insights.quote: Copper’s role in electrification: supply constraints and demand from EVs, grid infrastructure and datacentres.
